record.title: The 3-rank conjecture for matching complexes
record.statement:
For $k\geq 0$, consider the reduced homology group $\tilde{H}_{k+1}(\mathsf{M}_{2k+7};\mathbb{Z})$, where $\mathsf{M}_n$ denotes the matching complex on $n$ vertices. **The 3-rank conjecture.** The group is the direct sum of a free group and an elementary $3$-group of rank

$$
\binom{2k+6}{k}.
$$

The conjecture refines the known examples of 3-torsion in matching-complex homology by predicting its exact rank; no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Jakob Jonsson, “More Torsion in the Homology of the Matching Complex”, arXiv:1203.5658 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.5658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2012).

record.title: Non-D-finiteness conjecture for generating functions of colored set partitions
record.statement:
Let $C_n(r)$ denote the number of colored set partitions of $[n]$ with colors from a set of size $r$. A formal power series is **D-finite** if it satisfies a linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. **Non-D-finiteness conjecture.** The generating function

$$
\sum_{n\geq 0} C_n(r)x^n
$$

is not D-finite for integers $r\geq 3$. This is motivated by computational evidence for $r=3$ and by analogous results and heuristics for uncolored noncrossing partitions; the conjecture asserts that no such differential equation exists for any number of colors at least three.
record.source_name: Eric Marberg, “Crossings and nestings in colored set partitions”, arXiv:1203.5738 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.5738

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2012).

record.title: PFR conjecture in $\mathbb{Z}_m^n$
record.statement:
Let $m\geq 2$, let $n\geq 1$, and let $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_m^n$. Define the difference set by

$$
A-A=\{a_1-a_2:a_1,a_2\in A\}.
$$

**PFR conjecture.** If $|A-A|\leq\lambda|A|$, then there is a subgroup $H\leq\mathbb{Z}_m^n$ with $|H|\leq|A|$ such that $A$ is covered by $\lambda'=\lambda^{c_m}$ translates of $H$, where $c_m$ depends only on $m$. This is the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture in the finite abelian groups $\mathbb{Z}_m^n$; the paper uses it to derive stronger upper bounds for matching vector families when $m$ is fixed and $n$ grows, but its resolution status is not given here.
record.source_name: Abhishek Bhowmick, Zeev Dvir and Shachar Lovett, “New Lower Bounds for Matching Vector Codes”, arXiv:1204.1367 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1367

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2012).

record.title: Bounded-diameter conjecture for commuting graphs of centerless finite groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group with trivial centre, and let its **commuting graph** be the graph whose vertices are the non-central elements of $G$, with two distinct vertices adjacent exactly when they commute in $G$. **Centerless commuting-graph conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $d$ such that the commuting graph of $G$ is either disconnected or has diameter at most $d$. This is proposed after the unrestricted conjecture is disproved by finite special $2$-groups with commuting graphs of arbitrarily large diameter; the status of the centerless case is left open in the paper.
record.source_name: Michael Giudici and Chris Parker, “There is no upper bound for the diameter of the commuting graph of a finite group”, arXiv:1210.0348 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.0348

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2012).

record.title: Existence of a nonrepetitive palindrome-free sequence avoiding two subsequences
record.statement:
Let an infinite sequence be a sequence whose terms are drawn from the four-letter alphabet $\{A,B,C,D\}$. A sequence is **nonrepetitive** if it contains no contiguous block of the form $XX$ for a nonempty finite word $X$, and **palindrome-free** if it contains no nonempty palindromic contiguous block. It avoids the subsequences $CD$ and $DC$ if neither of these occurs as a subsequence.

**Sequence existence conjecture.** There exists an infinite sequence on four letters, $A,B,C$ and $D$ such that the sequence is nonrepetitive, palindrome-free and avoids the subsequences $CD$ and $DC$.

The paper states that this conjecture was recently confirmed by Kozik, so the existence claim is resolved.
record.source_name: Balázs Keszegh, Balázs Patkós and Xuding Zhu, “Nonrepetitive colorings of lexicographic product of graphs”, arXiv:1210.5607 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.5607

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2012); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Total sequence list 1-2-3 Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be any graph, and fix an ordering of the edges and vertices used in a total weighting. A **total sequence $k$-list-weighting** assigns to each edge and vertex a weight from its independently assigned list of $k$ real numbers; the induced vertex sequence records the relevant incident edge and vertex weights in the prescribed order. Let $\operatorname{ch}_\sigma^t(G)$ be the least $k$ such that every such list assignment permits adjacent vertices to receive different sequences. **The total sequence list 1-2-3 Conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{ch}_\sigma^t(G)\leq 2.
$$

This is the total sequence version of the list 1-2-3 problem. The surrounding discussion gives a general upper bound of $3$, while the stated bound $2$ is left as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Ben Seamone and Brett Stevens, “Sequence variations of the 1-2-3 Conjecture and irregularity strength”, arXiv:1211.0463 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.0463

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

record.title: Hansen–Li–Liu conjecture on the revised Szeged–Wiener difference for nonbipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with $n \geq 4$ vertices, $m \geq n$ edges, and an odd cycle. The **Hansen–Li–Liu conjecture.** asserts that

$$
Sz^*(G)-W(G) \geq \frac{n^2+4n-6}{4}.
$$

Moreover, the bound should be best possible, attained by the graph composed of a cycle on $3$ vertices, $C_3$, and a tree $T$ on $n-3$ vertices sharing a single vertex. Here $W(G)$ is the Wiener index and $Sz^*(G)$ is the revised Szeged index. The conjecture proposes a sharp lower bound for their difference among connected nonbipartite graphs with at least as many edges as vertices.
record.source_name: Lily Chen, Xueliang Li and Mengmeng Liu, “The (revised) Szeged index and the Wiener index of a nonbipartite graph”, arXiv:1211.5457 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.5457

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

record.title: Clique–Stable Set separation conjecture for graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. A **clique–stable set separator** is a family of cuts such that every disjoint clique and stable set of $G$ are separated by one of the cuts. **Clique–Stable Set separation conjecture.** There is a polynomial $Q$ such that every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices has a CS-separator of size at most

$$
Q(n).
$$

The source says that this positive formulation is generally believed to be false, while establishing such separators for several graph classes. Its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nicolas Bousquet, Aurélie Lagoutte and Stéphan Thomassé, “Clique versus Independent Set”, arXiv:1301.2474 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2474

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2013). “Huang and Sudakov proposed in a counterexample to the Alon-Saks-Seyour conjecture (then generalized in ), twenty-five years after its statement.”

record.title: Shephard–Kalai conjecture on subpolytopes of stacked polytopes
record.statement: Let $d\ge 0$. A **subpolytope** of a polytope is the convex hull of a subset of its vertices, and a **stacked polytope** is a polytope obtained by starting with a simplex and successively stacking simplices onto facets. **Shephard–Kalai conjecture.** Every combinatorial type of $d$-dimensional polytope can be realized using subpolytopes of $d$-dimensional stacked polytopes. This conjecture is the combinatorial version of Shephard's question whether every polytope is a subpolytope of some stacked polytope; the geometric question was disproved by Shephard, while the combinatorial assertion remains open here.
record.source_name: Karim Alexander Adiprasito and Arnau Padrol, “A universality theorem for projectively unique polytopes and a conjecture of Shephard”, arXiv:1301.2960 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2960

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Bounds on the critical interaction strength for graphs with one negative edge
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph with $N$ vertices, let $\Gamma_+$ denote its positive-edge subgraph, and let $t^\star(\Gamma)$ be the critical interaction strength at which stability is lost. Assume that $\Gamma_+$ is connected and that the negative-edge subgraph has exactly one edge. **Critical-strength bounds.** These are the extreme cases; for any graph $\Gamma$ satisfying these assumptions,

$$
t^\star(\Gamma) \in [(N-1)^{-1},(N-2)/2].
$$

The bounds are motivated by the ring and complete graph examples, but the source provides no resolution of whether they are sharp in a broader sense.
record.source_name: Jared C. Bronski and Lee DeVille, “Spectral Theory for Networks with Attractive and Repulsive Interactions”, arXiv:1303.0718 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0718

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2013).

record.title: Conjecture on contributions in simple matrices
record.statement:
Let a simple $m\times n$ $(0,1)$ matrix be a matrix with pairwise distinct columns, and let a contribution mean the configuration defined earlier in the paper. **Contribution conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that every simple matrix with $\lfloor c m^{k-1}\rfloor$ columns makes $m^{k-1}$ contributions:

$$
\text{every simple }m\times\lfloor c m^{k-1}\rfloor\text{ matrix makes }m^{k-1}\text{ contributions}.
$$

The authors state that this stronger assertion would imply the Anstee–Frankl–Füredi–Pach conjecture. The source does not indicate that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Arès Méroueh, “On Forbidden Submatrices”, arXiv:1401.2102 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.2102

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: Existence of non-isomorphic graphs with equal homomorphism polynomial
record.statement:
Let $q$ be fixed, and let $\mathcal{P}_q(G)$ denote the homomorphism polynomial of a graph $G$. Two graphs are **non-isomorphic** if there is no graph isomorphism between them. **Homomorphism-polynomial conjecture.** For any fixed $q$ there exist non-isomorphic graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ such that

$$
\mathcal{P}_q(G_1)=\mathcal{P}_q(G_2).
$$

The claim asserts that no fixed number of states $q$ determines every graph through its homomorphism polynomial. The paper notes that rotor-type constructions known for the Tutte polynomial and the bivariate Ising polynomial do not establish this claim, but presents it as a strong belief.
record.source_name: Klas Markström, “From the Ising and Potts models to the general graph homomorphism polynomial”, arXiv:1401.6335 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.6335

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: The shifted polygon setup perimeter-to-area conjecture
record.statement: A **shifted $(k,n)$-setup** is a configuration of $k$ regular polygons with $n$ vertices and unit side length, where the polygons are shifted as in the paper. Let $k$ and $n$ be coprime natural numbers. The **shifted polygon setup conjecture.** The perimeter-to-area ratio of a shifted $(k,n)$-setup is greater than the ratio in the case of a single regular $n$-gon with unit side length if and only if $k>1$ and $k\equiv 1\pmod n$. This gives a proposed characterization of exactly when the shifted construction improves on the single regular polygon; the statement is presented as an open problem based on computer experiments, and no proof or disproof is supplied.
record.source_name: Viktor Kiss and Zoltán Vidnyánszky, “Unions of regular polygons with large perimeter-to-area ratio”, arXiv:1402.5452 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.5452

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The full-rank coding conjecture for in-order streaming
record.statement: Let $s_1,s_2,\ldots$ be the source packets, let $V[n]$ be the transmit index in slot $n$, and suppose that a transmission with index $V[n]$ is a linear combination of source packets. Since packets must be decoded in order, the relevant class of transmissions consists of combinations of the packets $s_1$ through $s_{V[n]}$. **Full-rank coding conjecture.** Given transmit index $V[n]$, there is no loss of generality in including all packets $s_1$ to $s_{V[n]}$. This would justify restricting attention to full-rank codes, in which each transmission combines all packets up to its transmit index; the source presents this as a belief rather than an established result, and its effect on the achievable throughput–delay trade-off remains to be verified.
record.source_name: Gauri Joshi, Yuval Kochman and Gregory Wornell, “The Effect of Block-wise Feedback on the Throughput-Delay Trade-off in Streaming”, arXiv:1403.0259 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.0259

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2014).

record.title: The cap-induced factorization conjecture for even-dimensional projective spaces
record.statement: An $M$-cap in $\mathrm{PG}(n,q)$ is a set of $M$ points with no three collinear. By Ebert's theorem, if $n\geq 2$ is even, then $\mathrm{PG}(2n-1,q)$ can be partitioned into disjoint $M$-caps, where $M=q^n+1$. **Cap-induced factorization conjecture.** There exists an $(M-1)$-factorization of $\lambda K_v$, where $v=\tfrac{q^{2n}-1}{q-1}$, for some $\lambda$ induced by this set of $M$-caps, when $n\geq 2$ is even. This is a proposed construction of graph factorizations from cap partitions in finite projective spaces; the source does not provide a resolution.
record.source_name: György Kiss and Christian Rubio-Montiel, “A note on m-factorizations of complete multigraphs arising from designs”, arXiv:1407.5480 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5480

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: The 3-colorability conjecture for triangle- and ISK4-free graphs
record.statement: Here graphs are simple and finite. A graph is **triangle-free** if it contains no triangle and **ISK4-free** if it contains no induced subdivision of $K_4$, where $K_4$ is the complete graph on four vertices. A graph is 3-colorable if its vertices can be colored with three colors so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. **The 3-colorability conjecture for triangle- and ISK4-free graphs.** Every triangle-free, ISK4-free graph is 3-colorable. The paper states that this conjecture follows from the preceding low-degree vertex conjecture and proves both conjectures for graphs of girth at least $5$; the unrestricted case remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nicolas Trotignon and Kristina Vušković, “On triangle-free graphs that do not contain a subdivision of the complete graph on four vertices as an induced subgraph”, arXiv:1407.6531 (2014).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1308.6678](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.6678).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6531

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: Broersma's degree condition conjecture for hamiltonian claw-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 2-connected claw-free graph on $n$ vertices. An **end-vertex** of an induced copy of $N$ in $G$ is a vertex serving as an end-vertex in that copy.

**Broersma's conjecture.** If every end-vertex of an induced copy of $N$ in $G$ has degree at least $(n-2)/3$, then $G$ is hamiltonian.

This conjecture concerns degree conditions guaranteeing hamiltonicity in 2-connected claw-free graphs. The paper notes that it remains open; its results establish the analogous assertion with the stronger bound $|V(G)|/3+1$, giving an affirmative solution up to an additive constant.
record.source_name: Roman Čada, Binlong Li, Bo Ning and Shenggui Zhang, “Induced subgraphs with large degrees at end-vertices for hamiltonicity of claw-free graphs”, arXiv:1409.4585 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.4585

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2014). “This conjecture is still open.”

record.title: Contractible p-component conjecture for the $(d-1)$-st Beer index
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 2$, let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ be a set whose $(d-1)$-st Beer index $\operatorname{b}_{d-1}(S)$ is defined, and assume that every p-component of $S$ is contractible. Let $\operatorname{c}(S)$ denote the index of convexity. **Contractible p-component conjecture.** There is a constant $\alpha=\alpha(d)>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{b}_{d-1}(S)\leq\alpha\operatorname{c}(S).
$$

This proposes a higher-dimensional analogue of the planar linear upper bound, replacing simple connectivity by contractibility of every p-component. The statement is presented as a possible generalization and remains open.
record.source_name: Martin Balko, Vít Jelínek, Pavel Valtr and Bartosz Walczak, “On the Beer index of convexity and its variants”, arXiv:1412.1769 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.1769

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

record.title: The complete-bipartite extremal conjecture for algebraic connectivity
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with exactly $n$ vertices and $m=2(n-2)$ edges. The **complete-bipartite extremal conjecture.** Among all such graphs, a graph maximizing the algebraic connectivity is the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,n-2}$, and

$$
\lambda_{2}(K_{2,n-2})=2.
$$

This conjecture concerns the graph with four fewer edges than the complete bipartite graph parameterized by its smaller part. The source presents it as an open conjecture motivated by numerical and extremal questions about maximizing algebraic connectivity.
record.source_name: Theodore Kolokolnikov, “Maximizing algebraic connectivity for certain families of graphs”, arXiv:1412.6147 (2014).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6147

record.title: Component spanning trees avoiding any prescribed label
record.statement: Let $\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{2n+1}$ be the graph whose components $A$ have labeled edges, and let $\eta$ be a label of a component $A$. A **component spanning tree** of $A$ is a spanning tree using vertices of $A$ and edges of the component. **Label-avoiding spanning-tree conjecture.** For each component $A$ in $\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{2n+1}$, with $n\geq 3$, and for each label $\eta$ of $A$, there exists a component spanning tree of $A$ containing no edge with label $\eta$. This assertion would provide the nearly spanning trees needed by the proposed snake construction, but the source does not report a proof for general $n$.
record.source_name: Michal Horovitz and Tuvi Etzion, “Constructions of Snake-in-the-Box Codes for Rank Modulation”, arXiv:1311.4703 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.4703

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).
